fatal_errors: The proposed polycrystalline titanium alloy is unrelated to the target equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single crystals.
The loading mode, specimen state, orientation, and temperature window do not reconstruct the compression study conducted from 9 to 1373 K.

The monotonic prediction of increasing plastic deformation with temperature misses the observed cryogenic CRSS increase and inertial dulling, as well as the high-temperature Portevin-Le Chatelier strengthening peak and serrated flow.
The hypothesis omits the central composition-dependent mechanisms: MSAD-controlled solid-solution strengthening, phonon-drag-controlled dislocation inertia, and Mn/Fe-associated Cottrell pinning.
explanation: The response only aligns at the generic level that temperature affects dislocation-mediated plasticity. Room temperature is a relevant baseline, and temperature-dependent mechanical testing could test a broad titanium-alloy claim, but the proposed experiment lacks strain-rate jumps, CRSS/slip-system analysis, TEM, and lattice-distortion measurements needed to distinguish the target mechanisms. Grain-boundary sliding and diffusion are not the principal mechanisms established for the target bulk single crystals. The material choice, conditions, predicted trend, compositional relationships, and mechanistic interpretation therefore fail to reconstruct the hidden study, while the absence of evidence also leaves the alternative titanium hypothesis unsupported.
